solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Murder is detective's province

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, so DI'S is the detective's
a patch is someone's area of responsibility, their province

explanation.surface: A claim that killings fall squarely within a police officer's sphere of work.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as DI'S PATCH: the inspector's territory.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch someone is to kill them, a common euphemism for murder.

clue.text: Stop taking sides, recklessly heading for trouble

indicators.note: recklessly suggests the letters of sides thrown about carelessly
heading for takes the first letter of trouble

explanation.surface: An appeal to stop picking sides rashly before it ends in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recklessly' rearranges SIDES into DESIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or stop doing something.

clue.text: Embarrassed sailor boy coming aboard scruffy

indicators.note: the sailor and boy come aboard, inside, the word for embarrassed

parts.note: shy means bashful, embarrassed
AB is an able seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: An embarrassed young sailor boarding ship looking untidy.
explanation.walkthrough: SH(AB B)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby clothes or people look worn and untidy, scruffy.

clue.text: See you in France — you said to follow crazy idea!

indicators.note: the letter comes after the rearranged idea
crazy suggests the letters of idea in a mad jumble
said means spoken, so the word is replaced by a letter heard the same

parts.note: the word you, spoken, is heard as the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone calls a mad idea farewell in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' turns IDEA into ADIE; 'said' turns YOU into U.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for goodbye, roughly 'see you', a farewell.

clue.text: Approach prisoner with discretion

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
tact is discretion in dealing with others

explanation.surface: Advice to deal with an inmate tactfully.
explanation.walkthrough: CON + TACT.
explanation.definitionFit: To contact someone is to approach or get in touch with them.

clue.text: Sailor has uniform tucked in and eyes front to show respect

indicators.note: the uniform's letter is tucked inside the sailor's word

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: eyes front takes just the leading letter of eyes

explanation.surface: A sailor in neat uniform, eyes front, standing respectfully on parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eyes front' sounds like a parade-ground order but supplies E.
explanation.definitionFit: A salute is a gesture made to show respect, especially to a superior officer.

clue.text: Something only a fool would do, like admitting fix over match

definitions.text: Something only a fool would do

indicators.note: the like word admits, lets in, the reversed letters

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: over turns the fix word round to read backwards

parts.note: gum fixes things in place
a game is a match

explanation.surface: Match-fixing is a foolish enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses GUM to MUG; A(MUG)S + GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug's game is an idiom for an activity unlikely to bring any reward; a mug is a dupe.

clue.text: Entire organisation's bankrupt by November

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations Organisation; the 's is just glue
broke means penniless, bankrupt
November is N in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A whole organisation going bust by the end of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: UN + BROKE + N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbroken is whole and intact, entire.

clue.text: Use drill

definitions.meaning: to ... a right or power is to use it

explanation.surface: Use drill
explanation.walkthrough: Two short definitions: a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercise means both employing something and a training routine such as drill.

clue.text: Stops lads eating junk and fries essentially

indicators.note: the lads' word swallows the other letters, as if eating them

parts.note: sons are lads, boys
tat is cheap junk

indicators.note: the essence of fries is its central letter

explanation.surface: Young men stopping at a takeaway for junk food and chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stops' reads as a verb but is the plural noun; 'eating' and 'essentially' are the indicators, the latter taking the central I of fries.
explanation.definitionFit: Stations are stopping places on a railway or bus route.

clue.text: Miss fellow cutting head in fall

indicators.note: the fellow's letter cuts out and takes the place of the head of the word for fall

parts.note: a tumble is a fall

explanation.surface: A man stumbling and taking a header in a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: F replaces the T at the front of TUMBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fumble a catch is to miss it, handling it clumsily.

clue.text: Knit up edge round top of sweater

indicators.note: the reversed edge goes round the next letter
in a down clue, up means the edge word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a hem is the edge of a garment

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter of sweater

explanation.surface: Knitting up the edging around the neck of a jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses HEM to MEH, round S.
explanation.definitionFit: To mesh is to fit together or interlock, as knit does in 'knit together'.

clue.text: Put down sandwich container and brewed tea

parts.note: a sub is a submarine sandwich
a jug is a container for liquids

indicators.note: brewed suggests the letters of tea being stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone setting down their lunch, a jug and freshly made tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' rearranges TEA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To put down a rebellion or a people is to subjugate them, bring them under control.

clue.text: Holy woman's heartily rejoicing, bearing suffering without complaint

parts.note: ST, saint, a holy woman; the 's is possessive glue

indicators.note: heartily points to the heart, the central letters, of rejoicing

explanation.surface: A saintly woman rejoicing heartily even while enduring pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartily' takes the middle three letters OIC from REJOICING.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic is a person who endures pain or hardship calmly, like the philosophers of that school.

clue.text: Talk with bowler perhaps, following century

indicators.note: the hat comes after the century letter in the answer

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century
a bowler is a kind of hat, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: A cricket conversation with the bowler after a batsman's hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture misleads: the bowler is the hat, not the player.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat is an informal talk or conversation.

clue.text: Try and teach relaxation for pain

parts.note: a judge hears, or tries, a case

indicators.note: relaxation loosens the letters of teach into a new order

explanation.surface: Trying to teach relaxation techniques to ease suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxation' rearranges TEACH into TACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional anguish, a kind of pain.

clue.text: One's cross, drawn into horseplay with practical jokers

indicators.note: the letters are pulled inside the shuffled letters
play signals letters of horse moving freely into a new arrangement

parts.note: A means one
an X is a cross

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at getting dragged into rough horseplay by pranksters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horseplay' splits into HORSE and the anagram signal 'play', giving HOERS; 'drawn into' places A X inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoaxers are tricksters who play hoaxes, deceptions done for a laugh.

clue.text: Problem with mission no-one raised

parts.note: a quest is a mission

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: NO and I for one

explanation.surface: A troubled mission that nobody took up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses NO + I to ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A question can be a problem or matter at issue, as in 'a question of money'.

clue.text: Dashed good work everyone put in on education

indicators.note: the everyone word is put in between the other two

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
all means everyone
ED is short for education; in a down clue, the link 'on' places it after

explanation.surface: A school report praising the effort everyone put into learning.
explanation.walkthrough: G(ALL)OP + ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallop is to run fast like a horse, so galloped means dashed.

clue.text: Not knowing French, article's a struggle to penetrate

indicators.note: A WAR must penetrate, go inside, the French word

parts.note: UNE is the French feminine indefinite article
a war is a struggle

explanation.surface: Someone ignorant of French struggling with a news article.
explanation.walkthrough: UN(A WAR)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unaware means lacking knowledge of something, ignorant of it.

clue.text: Regret turning up with zero cash abroad

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A traveller regretting arriving with no money overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses RUE to EUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the currency used across much of Europe, cash spent abroad by Britons.

clue.text: Sketched Doctor with bridge partners

parts.note: East and West are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: An artist sketched a doctor accompanied by a bridge pair.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South and East-West play as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Drew is the past tense of draw, so it means sketched.

clue.text: Record in old collection has soldiers' lament

indicators.note: the record goes in among the rearranged letters
collection means the letters of old gathered up and rearranged

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: A record from an old album holding a soldiers' lament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collection' is the anagram signal, not a noun: it gathers the letters into DLO, and 'in' puts the record inside after the D. The Royal Engineers are a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplore something is to lament it or express strong disapproval.

clue.text: Old Queen caught posh gal acting common

indicators.note: the queen's letters catch the others inside them

parts.note: VR is Victoria Regina, Queen Victoria
U means upper-class, posh

indicators.note: acting suggests the letters of gal playing a different part

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria noticing a well-bred girl behaving coarsely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acting' rearranges GAL to LGA; V(U LGA)R.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulgar means coarse or lacking refinement, common.

clue.text: Vegetable from marsh eaten primarily in the Netherlands

parts.note: a fen is a marsh

indicators.note: that letter goes in the country code

parts.note: NL is the international code for the Netherlands

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of eaten

explanation.surface: A vegetable grown in Dutch marshland and eaten mostly there.
explanation.walkthrough: FEN + N(E)L.
explanation.definitionFit: Fennel is an aniseed-flavoured plant whose bulb is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Get quietly drunk after parents finally divorce

indicators.note: the quiet and drunk letters come after the parents' last letter
finally takes the last letter of parents

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone quietly getting drunk once their parents' marriage ends.
explanation.walkthrough: S + P + LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples who split up have separated, as in a divorce.

clue.text: Photocopy amendment to procedure

indicators.note: an amendment changes the word procedure, here rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: An office instruction to copy the change to a procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amendment to' rearranges PROCEDURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproduce a document is to make a copy of it, as a photocopier does.

clue.text: Old quarter has a bit of atmosphere

parts.note: a zone is a district or quarter

explanation.surface: An old district of town with a certain charm.
explanation.walkthrough: O + ZONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a gas found in a layer of the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: Collision has traffic, initially better on motorway, turned back

indicators.note: the assembled letters are turned to read backwards
initially takes the first letter of traffic

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A crash involving traffic that was flowing better on the motorway, then turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: T + CAP + MI reads backwards as the answer. The M1 runs from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: An impact is the forceful striking of one thing against another, a collision.

clue.text: Boot gang off sledge

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of boot gang going wrong, scrambled

explanation.surface: An order to kick a gang off a sledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges BOOTGANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A toboggan is a long, light sled used for sliding down snowy slopes.

clue.text: Agreed to recycle odds and ends sons left out

indicators.note: recycling reprocesses the letters of odds and ends into a new form
the two S letters are left out of the pool

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, so two sons are SS

explanation.surface: A decision to recycle bits and pieces, once the sons had been excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: ODDS + ENDS rearranged, less two S's, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding the head is a sign of assent, so someone who nodded agreed.

clue.text: Intellectual from CERN abridged book, cutting real analysis

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, losing the last letter

parts.note: CERN is the European particle physics laboratory

indicators.note: the book letter cuts into the rearranged letters
analysis breaks the word real down and reassembles its letters

explanation.surface: A shortened book from the physics lab, with its own breakdown of reality.
explanation.walkthrough: CER + E(B)RAL, where ERAL is the anagram of REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebral describes someone of the intellect rather than the emotions, an intellectual type.
